name: Netherlands
governanceModel: Active AI diplomacy paired with new domestic AI Act implementation under a decentralized regulator model
debateTopics: Diplomatic activity without a domestic AI champion
overview:
Following the formation of the Jetten cabinet (D66, VVD and CDA) on 23 February 2026, the Netherlands has continued to position itself as an active diplomatic voice on AI even without a flagship national AI lab of its own. In July 2026 it submitted an International AI Strategy to parliament — built on diplomatic effort, new coalitions, and strengthening European AI capacity — led by State Secretary for Digital Economy and Sovereignty Willemijn Aerdts (Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate) alongside the Ministers of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade.

Domestically, Aerdts also put a Dutch AI Implementation Act out for public consultation in April 2026 — legislation intended to transpose EU AI Act supervision and enforcement obligations into Dutch national law via a decentralized model of sectoral regulators, rather than a single dedicated AI authority. A significant AI-adjacent industrial asset is ASML, whose lithography machines are essential to the global AI chip supply chain, even though ASML itself isn't an AI company.

debates.topic: Diplomatic leadership without a domestic AI champion
debates.summary: The Netherlands punches above its weight in AI diplomacy but has no flagship frontier lab comparable to Mistral or Google DeepMind.
debates.expanded: The International AI Strategy positions the Netherlands as a coalition-builder and European AI capacity advocate, a role that doesn't require a domestic frontier lab. But it does raise the question of whether diplomatic leadership without commensurate domestic industrial capability is sustainable long-term, especially as neighbouring countries invest heavily in sovereign compute and national champions.

debates.summary: The consultation on national AI Act implementation legislation will determine what Dutch-specific obligations sit atop the EU-wide baseline.
debates.expanded: Like other member states, the Netherlands must designate national competent authorities and decide on enforcement mechanics for the AI Act. The Implementation Act consultation is where Dutch-specific choices — sanctions levels, sandbox design, sector-specific carve-outs — will be made.
